argument_summary: No new evidence is offered. The narrow defense is that the record supports a launch-readiness rationale for certification, not a clean showing that the materiality/disclosure predicate was resolved. Admissible evidence shows aggregate readiness cleared by 2.4 percentage points, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general governance support for documenting limitations and monitoring risk after launch. At the same time, the same admissible record shows a 1.5 percentage point miss in a segment named in a regulated-customer pilot order form, plus an open legal review. The appropriate interpretation is therefore weak, caveated support for the certification decision on aggregate-readiness grounds, while conceding the policy link the auditor identified remains unresolved on this record.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would delay the regulated-customer demo launch path. On the current admissible record, that cost should be weighed against the fact that there is some real launch-readiness support in evidence, even though the disclosure-or-acceptance predicate is unresolved.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not say aggregate readiness or monitoring alone satisfy the requirement for a material named use case. The 3% traffic note can inform prioritization, but under the stated policy it does not by itself defeat materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments and legal review is still open. We therefore are not claiming the record proves clean compliance. The narrower claim is that the certification rationale can be described accurately as a constrained, weakly supported judgment under uncertainty rather than as a fabricated or wholly unsupported decision.
concessions: The current record does not show that the named use case limitation was resolved before launch.
The current record does not show an approved pre-launch risk acceptance.
The current record does not show that a required disclosure was completed.
The open legal review leaves the disclosure obligation unresolved on the present evidence.
The 3% traffic figure does not, by itself, resolve materiality under the stated policy.
